title: Slovenia’s Janša helps Netanyahu blunt EU response to West Bank land‑grab
text:
EUobserver

EU and the World

Ljubljana has undercut European reaction to Israel’s drastic carve-up of the West Bank, signalling that Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu has a new inside man in Brussels – Slovenia’s populist prime minister Janez Janša.

Netanyahu’s decision to build a settlement in the strategic E1 area of the West Bank, cutting the region and the two-state solution in half, was due to have met with condemnation “on behalf of the European Union and its 27 member states” on 23 August.

But this was downgraded to a lower level, in protocol terms, to a statement by Kaja Kallas, the EU high representative for foreign affairs.

Kallas’ remarks were also larded with gratitude that “we [the EU] note the recent charges brought by the Israeli prosecutors against some perpetrators of such [West Bank] violence.”

Israel’s prosecutions have near-zero outcomes.

And the diplomatic downgrade was due to a veto by Slovenia of the full EU27-level statement, diplomatic sources said.

Netanyahu used to rely on Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán to routinely defang EU criticism.

Read more

But Orbán lost office in April, while Janša returned to power in May, and turned the country's Middle East policy upside down.

The new E1 construction was seen as such a grave development that Israel-friendly EU states, such as Austria, Germany, Greece, and Italy also spoke out forcefully against it this week.

And even Janša signed up to EU sanctions against Israeli firms if they dared to build E1 at an EU summit back in June, despite his pro-Israel rhetoric.

"The European Council stresses that businesses should not bid for construction contracts for E1 or other settlement developments and underlines the legal and reputational consequences for businesses participating in settlement construction, including the risk of serious breaches of international law," said the Janša co-signed EU summit text on 19 June 2026.

Meanwhile, his watering down of the EU statement on 23 August comes amid other signs of his deepening relations with Netanyahu's government.

Janša gave VIP treatment to a prominent Israeli settler extremist, Yossi Dagan, in Ljubljana on 15 June.

And an Israeli private-intelligence firm, Black Cube, tried to tip the scales in Janša's favour in Slovenia's May election.
